title: I wish + past
note: Past form, present meaning: I wish I had more time. Czech Kez bych. Target error *I wish I have. Same backward shift as b1_second_conditional, which plays immediately before, so the shift is recycled rather than re-explained (F1). wish + past perfect (regret about the past) stays at B2 in b2_wish_if_only. Thickened 10 -> 25 items 2026-09-04 (agent loop). New this pass: the wish/hope contrast, which is a real Czech interference point (prát si covers both) and also the fix for a lint artefact - `wish` appeared in no gap_answer, so the taught lexicon did not contain the unit's own headword and all ten items read as F3 leads. Five items now gap wish / wishes / hope, and they have their own intro card (C11). Also new: wish + would for someone else's behaviour, which card 4 already listed as a mistake and the bank never drilled, and the negative step-back (didn't have to). A4 clean. `loud` and `closer` swapped for taught words, which also took three types off the audit. KNOWN LINT FALSE POSITIVE: the six remaining A8 flags want *I wish I'd more time* as the twin of `I wish I had more time`. Lexical had does not contract; do not add those accepts. Same lint gap as b1_past_modals and b1_second_conditional, queued in DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: I wish + past
cards.title_cz: I wish + minulý tvar — kéž bych
points: The verb goes back one step, but the meaning is about **now**.

rows: I want it to be different **now**
I want to be able to, now

cards.title: wish or hope?
points: **hope** looks forward to something that can really happen.
**wish** looks at something that is not true now.

rows: she does not, and I want her to
it is raining, and I mind

cards.title: The same step back as the if sentence
cards.title_cz: Stejný krok zpět jako u věty s if
points: If the real sentence is negative, the wish is positive, and the other way round.

rows: **were** for every person, like the if phrase
heard in speech, but **were** is the set form

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: After **wish**, the verb steps back — never stays in the present.

rows: ~~I wish I would have a car.~~

items.en: I wish I had more time.
items.gap: I wish I ____ more time. (have)
accepts: I wish I had more time.
items.wrong: I wish I have more time.
items.explanation: **wish** + the past form **had**, even though it is about now.
items.explanation_cz: **wish** + minulý tvar **had**, i když jde o teď.

items.en: I wish I could speak Spanish.
items.gap: I wish I ____ speak Spanish. (can)
accepts: I wish I could speak Spanish.
items.wrong: I wish I can speak Spanish.
items.explanation: **can** steps back to **could** after wish.
items.explanation_cz: **can** se po wish posune na **could**.

items.en: She wishes she lived in Prague.
items.cz: Přeje si, aby bydlela v Praze.
items.gap: She wishes she ____ in Prague. (live)
accepts: She wishes she lived in Prague.
items.explanation: Past form **lived** for a present wish.
items.explanation_cz: Minulý tvar **lived** pro přání o přítomnosti.
items.wrong: She wishes she lives in Prague.

items.en: I wish I were taller.
items.gap: I wish I ____ taller. (be)
accepts: I wish I were taller.
items.explanation: **were** is the set form after wish, for every person.
items.explanation_cz: **were** je ustálený tvar po wish, pro každou osobu.

items.en: I wish it wasn't so cold.
items.gap: I wish it ____ so cold. (not / be)
accepts: I wish it wasn't so cold.
I wish it weren't so cold.
I wish it was not so cold.
I wish it were not so cold.
items.explanation: The real sentence is *it is cold*, so the wish is negative: **wasn't**.
items.explanation_cz: Skutečnost je *it is cold*, takže přání je záporné: **wasn't**.

items.en: I wish I knew his name.
items.gap: I wish I ____ his name. (know)
accepts: I wish I knew his name.
items.wrong: I wish I know his name.
items.explanation: **knew** — the point is that I do not know it now.
items.explanation_cz: **knew** — jde o to, že ho teď neznám.

items.en: They wish they had a bigger flat.
items.gap: They wish they ____ a bigger flat. (have)
accepts: They wish they had a bigger flat.
items.explanation: Past form **had** after wish, for a flat they do not have now.
items.explanation_cz: Minulý tvar **had** po wish, o bytě, který teď nemají.

items.en: I wish my flat wasn't so small.
items.cz: Kéž by můj byt nebyl tak malý.
items.gap: I wish my flat ____ so small. (not / be)
accepts: I wish my flat wasn't so small.
I wish my flat was not so small.
items.explanation: After **wish** the verb steps back: **wasn't**, not isn't.
items.explanation_cz: Po **wish** jde sloveso o krok zpět: **wasn't**, ne isn't.
items.wrong: I wish my flat isn't so small.

items.en: He wishes he could come with us.
items.cz: Přeje si, aby mohl jet s námi.
items.gap: He wishes he ____ come with us. (can)
accepts: He wishes he could come with us.
items.explanation: **can** becomes **could** after wish.
items.explanation_cz: **can** se po wish mění na **could**.

items.en: I wish I had a car.
items.gap: I wish I ____ a car. (have)
accepts: I wish I had a car.
items.wrong: I wish I would have a car.
items.explanation: **had**, not would have. would after wish is for asking someone to change.
items.explanation_cz: **had**, ne would have. would po wish se používá, když chceš, aby někdo něco změnil.

items.en: I hope you feel better tomorrow.
items.cz: Doufám, že ti bude zítra líp.
items.gap: I ____ you feel better tomorrow. (wish / hope)
accepts: I hope you feel better tomorrow.
items.wrong: I wish you feel better tomorrow.
items.explanation: **hope** looks forward to something that can really happen, and the verb after it stays normal.
items.explanation_cz: **hope** se dívá dopředu na něco, co se opravdu může stát, a sloveso za ním zůstává normální.

items.en: I hope it doesn't rain tomorrow.
items.gap: I ____ it doesn't rain tomorrow. (wish / hope)
accepts: I hope it doesn't rain tomorrow.
I hope it does not rain tomorrow.
items.wrong: I wish it doesn't rain tomorrow.
items.explanation: Tomorrow is still open, so this is **hope**. *wish* would need the past form and would mean it is hopeless.
items.explanation_cz: Zítřek je pořád otevřený, takže je to **hope**. *wish* by potřebovalo minulý tvar a znamenalo by, že je to beznadějné.

items.en: I hope you have a good weekend.
items.gap: I ____ you have a good weekend. (wish / hope)
accepts: I hope you have a good weekend.
I hope you've a good weekend.
items.wrong: I wish you have a good weekend.
items.explanation: A possible, ordinary future: **hope** + present. Not a wish about now.
items.explanation_cz: Možná, běžná budoucnost: **hope** + přítomný čas. Není to přání o teď.

items.en: I wish I had more money.
items.gap: I ____ I had more money. (wish / hope)
accepts: I wish I had more money.
items.wrong: I hope I had more money.
items.explanation: It is not true now and cannot simply happen, so it is **wish** — and the verb steps back to *had*.
items.explanation_cz: Teď to není pravda a nemůže se to prostě stát, takže je to **wish** — a sloveso jde zpět na *had*.

items.en: She wishes she had a garden.
items.gap: She ____ she had a garden. (wish / hope)
accepts: She wishes she had a garden.
items.wrong: She hopes she had a garden.
items.explanation: **wishes** with -s for she, and the past **had** after it. *hopes she had* is not English.
items.explanation_cz: **wishes** s -s pro she a za tím minulé **had**. *hopes she had* není angličtina.

items.en: I wish I didn't have to work on Saturday.
items.cz: Kéž bych nemusel v sobotu do práce.
items.gap: I wish I ____ have to work on Saturday. (not / do)
accepts: I wish I didn't have to work on Saturday.
I wish I did not have to work on Saturday.
items.wrong: I wish I don't have to work on Saturday.
items.explanation: The negative steps back too: **didn't** have to, not don't.
items.explanation_cz: I zápor jde o krok zpět: **didn't** have to, ne don't.

items.en: I wish they would listen to me.
items.gap: I wish they ____ to me. (will / would)
accepts: I wish they would listen to me.
I wish they'd listen to me.
items.wrong: I wish they will listen to me.
items.explanation: For someone else's behaviour that annoys you, **wish** takes **would** + plain verb.
items.explanation_cz: Když jde o chování někoho jiného, co tě štve, má **wish** tvar **would** + základní sloveso.

items.en: I wish you would help me.
items.gap: I wish you ____ me. (will / would)
accepts: I wish you would help me.
I wish you'd help me.
items.wrong: I wish you will help me.
items.explanation: **would help** — you could help and you are not. Never *will* after wish.
items.explanation_cz: **would help** — pomoct bys mohl a nepomáháš. Po wish nikdy *will*.

items.en: He wishes he had more free time.
items.cz: Přeje si mít víc volného času.
items.gap: He wishes he ____ more free time. (have)
accepts: He wishes he had more free time.
items.wrong: He wishes he has more free time.
items.explanation: **wishes** + the past **had**, even though he means now.
items.explanation_cz: **wishes** + minulé **had**, i když myslí teď.

items.en: We wish we could stay longer.
items.gap: We wish we ____ stay longer. (can)
accepts: We wish we could stay longer.
items.wrong: We wish we can stay longer.
items.explanation: *can* steps back to **could** after wish — there is no *would can*.
items.explanation_cz: *can* jde po wish zpět na **could** — žádné *would can* neexistuje.

items.en: She wishes she could drive.
items.gap: She wishes she ____ drive. (can)
accepts: She wishes she could drive.
items.wrong: She wishes she can drive.
items.explanation: **could** is the step-back form of can, and it does not change for she.
items.explanation_cz: **could** je krok zpět od can a pro she se nemění.

items.en: They wish they lived in a house.
items.gap: They wish they ____ in a house. (live)
accepts: They wish they lived in a house.
items.wrong: They wish they live in a house.
items.explanation: **lived** is the past form doing present work: they live in a flat now.
items.explanation_cz: **lived** je minulý tvar v přítomné roli: teď bydlí v bytě.

items.en: I wish my brother would call me.
items.gap: I wish my brother ____ me. (will / would)
accepts: I wish my brother would call me.
items.wrong: I wish my brother will call me.
items.explanation: Somebody else's behaviour again: **would call**.
items.explanation_cz: Zase chování někoho jiného: **would call**.

items.en: I wish I didn't work at weekends.
items.gap: I wish I ____ work at weekends. (not / do)
accepts: I wish I didn't work at weekends.
I wish I did not work at weekends.
items.wrong: I wish I don't work at weekends.
items.explanation: Step back in the negative: **didn't** work.
items.explanation_cz: Krok zpět i v záporu: **didn't** work.

items.en: I wish I could help you.
items.gap: I wish I ____ help you. (can)
accepts: I wish I could help you.
items.wrong: I wish I can help you.
items.explanation: **could** after wish — the step back from *can*, meaning I cannot.
items.explanation_cz: **could** po wish — krok zpět od *can*, znamená to, že nemůžu.
